runs.text: Five Israeli street names. Each one hides a secret meaning. Rothschild. <<ˈ|r|oʊ|t>> means red. <<ˈ|ʃ|ɪ|l|t>> means shield. In the fifteen hundreds, the family lived in a Frankfurt house with a red shield sign. The boulevard honours Baron Edmond de Rothschild. Ben Gurion was born David Groon. Groon means green. In nineteen ten, he took a new name, from a Jewish rebel against Rome. Sokolov. Sokol is Russian for falcon. Nahum Sokolov later led the World Zionist Organization. Kaplan comes from Latin. A cape, then a chaplain, a priest. Many Kaplan families are <<k|oʊ|h|ɑ|ˈ|n|i|m>>, Jewish priests. The street honours Israel's first finance minister. Ostrovsky. Ostrov means island. Most likely, the family came from a town called Ostrov. And in Raanana, the first mayor was Baruch Ostrovsky. So what does your surname mean? Tell me in the comments. Next time, read the street sign twice.
